# 1. Load & Prepare Data

```{r load-data}
load_cs <- function(path) {
  df <- read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  df$month <- as.Date(df$month)
  
  # Contiguous integer period index (1..T): dense rank of months. Replaces the
  # old YYYY*100+MM coding, which distorts dynamic event time at year boundaries
  # (Dec -> Jan jumps by 89). Built identically to the techtagged sibling.
  mfloor      <- as.Date(format(df$month, "%Y-%m-01"))
  u_periods   <- sort(unique(mfloor))
  period_idx  <- setNames(seq_along(u_periods), as.character(u_periods))
  df$period   <- as.integer(period_idx[as.character(mfloor)])

  # g_period on the same contiguous scale (0 = never-treated). Kept NUMERIC
  # (double), not integer: did recodes never-treated groups to Inf internally,
  # which an integer column cannot hold (-> NA -> rows dropped -> "No valid groups").
  df$g <- as.character(df$g)
  df$g[df$g == "" | df$g == "NA"] <- NA
  g_floor     <- as.Date(format(as.Date(df$g), "%Y-%m-01"))
  df$g_period <- period_idx[as.character(g_floor)]
  df$g_period[is.na(df$g_period)] <- 0L
  df$g_period <- as.numeric(df$g_period)
  
  # Firm ID as integer
  df$firm_id <- as.integer(factor(df$Linkedin_name))
  
  # Log outcome
  df$log_collabs <- log1p(df$n_collabs)
  
  df
}

battery_s1  <- load_cs(PATH_BATTERY_S1)
```

# 2. Callaway & Sant'Anna Estimation

```{r cs-function}
# Primary C&S control group: NEVER-TREATED for BOTH technologies (mirrors the
# techtagged sibling). Some firms are treated in multiple IPCEI rounds, so a
# not-yet-treated firm may already be affected by an earlier treatment and
# contaminate the control pool; never-treated controls avoid this and make the
# two technologies symmetric. (Battery is a single cohort, which independently
# requires never-treated.) The not-yet-treated alternative is one robustness row
# for hydrogen.
cg_for <- function(technology) "nevertreated"

run_cs <- function(df, yname = "log_collabs", label = "", xformla = NULL, control_group = "notyettreated", clustervars = NULL) {
  
  cat("\n=== C&S:", label, "===\n")
  
  # Deterministic per-outcome seed: makes every estimate reproducible and
  # independent of how many other outcomes ran earlier in the same session.
  # With a single set.seed() up front, adding one outcome shifts the bootstrap
  # stream for every later run and moves all downstream p-values.
  set.seed(42L + sum(utf8ToInt(paste0(yname, control_group))))
  cs_out <- att_gt(
    yname         = yname,
    tname         = "period",
    idname        = "firm_id",
    gname         = "g_period",
    control_group = control_group,
    clustervars   = clustervars,
    anticipation  = 0,
    bstrap        = TRUE,
    biters        = BITERS,
    panel         = TRUE,
    xformla       = xformla,
    pl            = TRUE,
    data          = df
  )
  
  print(summary(cs_out))
  cs_out
}
```

```{r cs-battery}
# Battery: single cohort → one ATT(g,t) per post-treatment period

cs_battery_s1 <- run_cs(battery_s1, label = "Battery Spec 1 (balance)", control_group = cg_for("battery"), clustervars = "firm_id")
cs_battery_s2 <- run_cs(battery_s2, label = "Battery Spec 2 (power)", control_group = cg_for("battery"), clustervars = "firm_id")
```

```{r cs-hydrogen}
cs_hydrogen_s2 <- run_cs(hydrogen_s2, label = "Hydrogen Spec 2 (power)", control_group = cg_for("hydrogen"), clustervars = "firm_id")
```

```{r cs-robustness}
# Robustness: not-yet-treated controls as one shown alternative to the primary
# never-treated choice. Hydrogen only -- battery is a single cohort with no
# not-yet-treated units (att_gt would fail "No valid groups"). Firm clustering
# is kept to match the primary spec.
cs_hydrogen_notyet <- run_cs(hydrogen_s1,
                             label = "Hydrogen (primary, not-yet-treated)",
                             control_group = "notyettreated",
                             clustervars = "firm_id")
```

```{r cs-aggregate}

agg_simple  <- function(cs_out) aggte(cs_out, type = "simple")
agg_dynamic <- function(cs_out) aggte(cs_out, type = "dynamic",
                                      min_e = -12, max_e = 24)

pval_from_att <- function(att, se) {
  round(2 * pnorm(-abs(att / se)), 3)
}

# Pre-trend test. Primary is did's universal Wald pre-test (cs_out$Wpval). For
# staggered designs that bootstrap covariance is singular and att_gt returns no
# Wald (hydrogen, confirmed -- it stays NULL under never- AND not-yet-treated).
# In that case fall back to a joint test that the pre-period (e < 0) dynamic
# event-study coefficients are zero: a chi-square of their t-statistics from
# aggte(type="dynamic") att.egt/se.egt (analytic SEs, df = # pre-periods). The
# `method` field records which test was used.
es_pretrend <- function(cs_out) {
  if (is.null(cs_out)) return(list(stat = NA_real_, p = NA_real_, method = NA_character_))
  if (!is.null(cs_out$Wpval))
    return(list(stat = round(cs_out$W, 3), p = round(cs_out$Wpval, 3), method = "Wald"))
  dyn <- tryCatch(
    aggte(cs_out, type = "dynamic", min_e = -12, max_e = 24, bstrap = FALSE, cband = FALSE),
    error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(dyn)) return(list(stat = NA_real_, p = NA_real_, method = NA_character_))
  pre <- dyn$egt < 0
  t2  <- (dyn$att.egt[pre] / dyn$se.egt[pre])^2
  ok  <- is.finite(t2); k <- sum(ok)
  if (k == 0) return(list(stat = NA_real_, p = NA_real_, method = NA_character_))
  stat <- sum(t2[ok])
  list(stat = round(stat, 3), p = round(1 - pchisq(stat, df = k), 3), method = "ES-joint")
}

sample_stats <- function(df, yname) {
  df_use <- df %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(.data[[yname]]),
      !is.na(firm_id),
      !is.na(period),
      !is.na(g_period)
    )

  data.frame(
    N_obs     = nrow(df_use),
    N_units   = n_distinct(df_use$firm_id),
    N_treated = n_distinct(df_use$firm_id[df_use$g_period > 0]),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

make_att_row <- function(agg_obj, label, type, cs_out = NULL, df = NULL, yname = NULL) {
  stats <- if (!is.null(df) && !is.null(yname)) {
    sample_stats(df, yname)
  } else {
    data.frame(N_obs = NA_integer_, N_units = NA_integer_, N_treated = NA_integer_)
  }

  pt <- es_pretrend(cs_out)
  data.frame(
    Specification    = label,
    Type             = type,
    ATT              = round(agg_obj$overall.att, 4),
    SE               = round(agg_obj$overall.se,  4),
    p_value          = pval_from_att(agg_obj$overall.att, agg_obj$overall.se),
    pretrend_stat    = pt$stat,
    pretrend_p_value = pt$p,
    pretrend_test    = pt$method,
    N_obs            = stats$N_obs,
    N_units          = stats$N_units,
    N_treated        = stats$N_treated,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

make_att_row_std <- function(agg_obj, technology, outcome, type,
                             cs_out = NULL, df = NULL, yname = NULL) {
  stats <- if (!is.null(df) && !is.null(yname)) {
    sample_stats(df, yname)
  } else {
    data.frame(N_obs = NA_integer_, N_units = NA_integer_, N_treated = NA_integer_)
  }

  pt <- es_pretrend(cs_out)
  data.frame(
    Technology       = technology,
    Outcome          = outcome,
    Type             = type,
    ATT              = round(agg_obj$overall.att, 4),
    SE               = round(agg_obj$overall.se,  4),
    p_value          = pval_from_att(agg_obj$overall.att, agg_obj$overall.se),
    pretrend_stat    = pt$stat,
    pretrend_p_value = pt$p,
    pretrend_test    = pt$method,
    N_obs            = stats$N_obs,
    N_units          = stats$N_units,
    N_treated        = stats$N_treated,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

# ── Primary specs: simple ATT ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
agg_battery_s1_simple  <- agg_simple(cs_battery_s1)
```

# 3. Power Simulation (Egerod & Hollenbach approach)

Simulate on real control-group data to preserve empirical variance and
autocorrelation structure, then inject an artificial ATT.

```{r power-function}
run_power_sim <- function(cs_data, att_true, n_sims = 200,
                          label = "", n_treated_target = NULL,
                          control_group = "notyettreated") {
  
  # Use only control firms as the empirical baseline
  controls_df <- cs_data[cs_data$is_control == 1, ]
  control_names <- unique(controls_df$Linkedin_name)
  n_controls    <- length(control_names)
  
  # Cohort structure: mimic real treated cohort timing
  real_cohorts <- cs_data %>%
    filter(is_treated == 1) %>%
    distinct(Linkedin_name, g_period) %>%
    count(g_period) %>%
    arrange(g_period)
  
  cat(sprintf("[%s] ATT=%.2f | Cohorts: %s\n",
              label, att_true,
              paste(real_cohorts$g_period, collapse = ", ")))
  
  results <- numeric(n_sims)
  
  for (i in seq_len(n_sims)) {
    
    if (i %% 25 == 0) { # shows whether R is alive during hibernation run
      cat(sprintf("[%s] simulation %d / %d\n", label, i, n_sims))
    }
    
    available <- control_names
    treated_pool <- character(0)
    g_vec        <- integer(0)
    
    # Sample from controls to fill each cohort
    for (k in seq_len(nrow(real_cohorts))) {
      n_k    <- real_cohorts$n[k]
      cohort <- real_cohorts$g_period[k]
      
      if (length(available) < n_k) break
      
      sampled    <- sample(available, n_k, replace = FALSE)
      available  <- setdiff(available, sampled)
      treated_pool <- c(treated_pool, sampled)
      g_vec        <- c(g_vec, rep(cohort, n_k))
    }
    
    # Assign groups
    g_lookup <- data.frame(Linkedin_name = treated_pool,
                           g_sim = g_vec,
                           stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    
    sim_treated <- controls_df %>%
      filter(Linkedin_name %in% treated_pool) %>%
      left_join(g_lookup, by = "Linkedin_name") %>%
      mutate(
        post_sim = as.integer(period >= g_sim),
        log_collabs_sim = log_collabs + att_true * post_sim,
        g_period_sim = g_sim,
        is_treated_sim = 1L
      )
    
    sim_controls <- controls_df %>%
      filter(Linkedin_name %in% available) %>%
      mutate(
        log_collabs_sim = log_collabs,
        g_period_sim    = 0L,
        is_treated_sim  = 0L
      )
    
    sim_data <- bind_rows(sim_treated, sim_controls) %>%
      mutate(firm_id_sim = as.integer(factor(Linkedin_name)))
    
    # Run C&S on simulated data
    result <- tryCatch({
      cs_sim <- att_gt(
        yname         = "log_collabs_sim",
        tname         = "period",
        idname        = "firm_id_sim",
        gname         = "g_period_sim",
        control_group = control_group,
        anticipation  = 0,
        bstrap        = FALSE,
        #biters        = 199,   # fewer iters for speed in simulation
        panel         = TRUE,
        print_details = FALSE,
        data          = sim_data
      )
      agg_sim <- aggte(cs_sim, type = "simple")
      z_stat  <- agg_sim$overall.att / agg_sim$overall.se
      as.integer(abs(z_stat) > 1.96)
    }, error = function(e) NA_integer_)
    
    results[i] <- result
  }
  
  mean(results, na.rm = TRUE)
}
```

```{r power-run, eval=RUN_POWER}
library(parallel)

# Robust parallelism: fork when available, but fall back to serial if the fork
# workers fail (e.g. a non-interactive session), so an overnight run never
# silently returns no results. Shadows parallel::mclapply for the calls below.
mclapply <- function(X, FUN, ..., mc.cores = min(4L, parallel::detectCores())) {
  res <- tryCatch(parallel::mclapply(X, FUN, ..., mc.cores = mc.cores),
                  error = function(e) base::lapply(X, FUN))
  if (any(vapply(res, function(z) inherits(z, "try-error"), logical(1))))
    res <- base::lapply(X, FUN)
  res
}

# ATT grid: effects of 5% to 30% increase in collaboration count
# On log scale: log(1 + effect) ≈ effect for small effects
att_grid <- log(1 + c(0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.25, 0.30))

# --- Hydrogen Spec 1 (balance) ---
cat("Running power simulation: Hydrogen Spec 1\n")
power_h_s1 <- unlist(
  mclapply(att_grid, function(a)
    run_power_sim(hydrogen_s1, a, n_sims = 200, label = "H-S1", control_group = cg_for("hydrogen")),
  mc.cores = 4)
)

# --- Hydrogen Spec 2 (power) ---
cat("Running power simulation: Hydrogen Spec 2\n")
power_h_s2 <- unlist(
  mclapply(att_grid, function(a)
    run_power_sim(hydrogen_s2, a, n_sims = 200, label = "H-S2", control_group = cg_for("hydrogen")),
  mc.cores = 4)
)

# --- Battery Spec 1 (balance) ---
cat("Running power simulation: Battery Spec 1\n")
power_b_s1 <- unlist(
  mclapply(att_grid, function(a)
    run_power_sim(battery_s1, a, n_sims = 200, label = "B-S1", control_group = cg_for("battery")),
  mc.cores = 4)
)

# --- Battery Spec 2 (power) ---
cat("Running power simulation: Battery Spec 2\n")
power_b_s2 <- unlist(
  mclapply(att_grid, function(a)
    run_power_sim(battery_s2, a, n_sims = 200, label = "B-S2", control_group = cg_for("battery")),
  mc.cores = 4)
)

power_results <- data.frame(
  att_pct       = round((exp(att_grid) - 1) * 100, 1),
  att_log       = round(att_grid, 3),
  power_h_s2    = round(power_h_s2, 3),   # primary first
  power_b_s2    = round(power_b_s2, 3),   # primary first
  power_h_s1    = round(power_h_s1, 3),   # robustness
  power_b_s1    = round(power_b_s1, 3)    # robustness
)

print(power_results)
write.csv(power_results, "../results/psm/intensity/power_simulation_results.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r power-plot, eval=RUN_POWER}
           hjust = 0) +

  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,1),
                     labels = scales::percent) +

  scale_colour_manual(values = c(
    "Hydrogen — primary (N=365)"    = "#1f77b4",
    "Battery — primary (N=224)"     = "#2ca02c",
    "Hydrogen — robustness (N=277)" = "#aec7e8",
    "Battery — robustness (N=168)"  = "#98df8a"
  )) +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(
    "Hydrogen — primary (N=365)"    = 1.1,
    "Battery — primary (N=224)"     = 1.1,
    "Hydrogen — robustness (N=277)" = 0.7,
    "Battery — robustness (N=168)"  = 0.7
  )) +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(
    "Hydrogen — primary (N=365)"    = 1,
    "Battery — primary (N=224)"     = 1,
    "Hydrogen — robustness (N=277)" = 0.5,
    "Battery — robustness (N=168)"  = 0.5
  )) +

  labs(
    x = "True treatment effect (% change in collaborations)",
    y = "Simulated Power",
    colour = NULL,
    shape = NULL,
    linewidth = NULL,
    alpha = NULL
    #title = "Power Simulation — C&S Estimator on Matched Samples",
    #caption = "200 simulation runs per ATT level. Baseline DGP from real control-group data."
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

print(p_power)

ggsave("../results/psm/intensity/power_simulation_plot.pdf",
       p_power,
       width = 9,
       height = 6)
```

# 5. Export long-format results (per-folder, for notebook 08)

Writes long-format CSVs into this file's own `results/intensity/` folder, mirroring
the `07_ck_didestimation_composition_techtagged` export schema, so notebook 08 can
read the overall-total ("intensity") reference outcome from a clean per-folder
source instead of the legacy `results/event_study_all.csv` / `results/att_summary_all.csv`.
The legacy writes above are intentionally KEPT until 08 is repointed and verified.

```{r export-intensity}
INTENSITY_TIME_UNIT <- "month"   # this file is monthly (YYYYMM coding); no quarterly toggle

# 1) Dynamic event study (long): one row per (Technology, Outcome, e).
#    SAME 95% CI convention (att +/- 1.96*se) and SAME "<Technology> -- <Outcome>"
#    label convention as the composition export, so 08 reads both identically.
export_dynamic <- function(agg_dyn, technology, outcome) {
  .crit <- if (!is.null(agg_dyn$crit.val.egt) && is.finite(agg_dyn$crit.val.egt))
    agg_dyn$crit.val.egt else qnorm(0.975)   # simultaneous band when available
  data.frame(
    label      = sprintf("%s -- %s", technology, outcome),
    Technology = technology,
    Outcome    = outcome,
    e          = agg_dyn$egt,
    att        = agg_dyn$att.egt,
    se         = agg_dyn$se.egt,
    ci_lower   = agg_dyn$att.egt - .crit * agg_dyn$se.egt,
    ci_upper   = agg_dyn$att.egt + .crit * agg_dyn$se.egt,
    TimeUnit   = INTENSITY_TIME_UNIT,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

# This file estimates a single outcome (total/intensity); export the primary-spec
# (S2) dynamic ATTs for battery and hydrogen.
event_study_intensity <- bind_rows(
  export_dynamic(agg_battery_s1_dyn,  "Battery",  "Total collabs"),
  export_dynamic(agg_hydrogen_s1_dyn, "Hydrogen", "Total collabs")
)

write.csv(event_study_intensity,
          "../results/psm/intensity/event_study_intensity.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# 2) Overall ATT summary in the SAME schema as att_techtagged_table.csv:
#    Technology, Outcome, Type, TimeUnit, ATT, SE, p_value, pretrend_*, N_*.
att_summary_intensity <- bind_rows(
  make_att_row_std(agg_battery_s1_simple,  "Battery",  "Total collabs", "Primary",
                   cs_out = cs_battery_s1,  df = battery_s1,  yname = "log_collabs"),
  make_att_row_std(agg_hydrogen_s1_simple, "Hydrogen", "Total collabs", "Primary",
                   cs_out = cs_hydrogen_s1, df = hydrogen_s1, yname = "log_collabs")
)
att_summary_intensity$TimeUnit <- INTENSITY_TIME_UNIT
att_summary_intensity <- att_summary_intensity[, c(
  "Technology", "Outcome", "Type", "TimeUnit", "ATT", "SE", "p_value",
  "pretrend_stat", "pretrend_p_value", "pretrend_test", "N_obs", "N_units", "N_treated"
)]

write.csv(att_summary_intensity,
          "../results/psm/intensity/att_summary_intensity.csv", row.names = FALSE)

cat("\n--- Per-folder intensity exports ---\n")
cat("event_study_intensity.csv:", nrow(event_study_intensity), "rows; labels:",
    paste(unique(event_study_intensity$label), collapse = " | "), "\n")
cat("att_summary_intensity.csv:", nrow(att_summary_intensity), "rows\n")
```

# Notes for paper

- **Outcome variable**: log_collabs — log-transformed monthly collaboration count. 
- **Estimator**: Callaway & Sant'Anna (2021, *Journal of Econometrics*),
  primary control group = never-treated (both technologies), firm-level clustered
  SEs, bootstrap inference (999 iterations); not-yet-treated shown as robustness.
- **Power simulation**: 150 runs per ATT level, DGP drawn from real control-group 
  data to preserve empirical variance and autocorrelation structure 
  (Egerod & Hollenbach 2024; Black et al. 2022).
- **Sensitivity**: Rosenbaum bounds (Rosenbaum 2002) using Wilcoxon signed-rank test. 
  Gamma threshold reported as the level of unmeasured confounding that would 
  render the pre-treatment balance test insignificant.
- **MDE interpretation**: Report minimum detectable effect in percent terms 
  (exp(MDE_log) - 1), which is directly interpretable as a % change in 
  monthly collaborations.
